title: A wait that gives up reads the pane and names the question on screen
action: D3 made herdr's `blocked` state bee's prompt detector. The live acceptance probe falsified its reach (D5): three concurrent agy runs into a genuinely untrusted workspace all sat at Antigravity's 'Do you trust this folder?' dialog while `herdr agent list` reported the agent as `idle`, never `blocked`. bee burned its whole 60s ready wait and failed with `agent never reported ready within 60s (ready-wait) — pane kept for inspection`, which says nothing about a question being on screen and sends the reader hunting the agent instead of the dialog. Add a DIAGNOSIS pass, and keep `blocked` exactly as it is for the fast path. (1) A pattern table beside `LIMIT_PATTERNS` (run.rs:61) — same house style, its own name, and a doc comment stating plainly that it is diagnosis-only and never load-bearing: it never decides whether to wait, only what to SAY once a wait has already given up, so a false positive costs a slightly wrong sentence and nothing else. (2) CRITICAL constraint on the patterns, learned from the live pane: a worker pane split three deep off the same parent came out about EIGHT COLUMNS wide, and `herdr pane read` returned the dialog clipped to `Do you t`, `Yes, I`, `No, ex`, one fragment per line. A long needle like `do you trust this folder` matches NOTHING there. Choose short, distinctive tokens that survive column clipping — the navigation hint `↑/↓`, `y/n`, `[y/N]`, `[Y/n]`, a selection caret, a line ending in a question mark — and say in the comment WHY they are short. (3) Wire the pass into every wait that gives up: the ready-gate timeout, delivery's `NeverAcked` (both bounds), and the round poll's idle timeout. Each reads the pane on its way out via the existing `pane_read` seam (run.rs:373) and, on a match, replaces its generic message with one that names the pane id, quotes the matched line verbatim, and states the remedy — answer the prompt in that pane, or pre-authorize whatever it is asking so the agent stops asking. On no match, the existing message is kept unchanged. A `pane_read` failure must never turn a real timeout into a different error: fall back to the generic message. (4) Do not touch `LIMIT_PATTERNS`, `find_limit_match`, or the paused-limit path — a usage-limit pause keeps its own behaviour and its own message. Tests: a clipped narrow-pane dialog capture producing the question-named error at the ready gate; the same at delivery's NeverAcked and at the round poll's idle timeout; a pane whose text matches nothing keeping the generic message byte-for-byte; a failing `pane_read` keeping the generic message; and the `blocked` fast paths still firing before any of this.

truths: A ready-gate timeout against a pane showing a question names the question and the remedy, not just the timeout
The same diagnosis runs at delivery's NeverAcked and at the round poll's idle timeout
The patterns survive an eight-column clipped pane capture
A non-matching pane or a failing pane_read leaves the existing message unchanged

artifacts.substantive: diagnosis-only pattern table with the clipping rationale, wired into three give-up paths, plus the tests above; no TODO stubs

key_links: the diagnosis pass runs only after a wait has already failed, never as a wait condition
prohibitions: The pattern table must never decide whether to keep waiting
No change to LIMIT_PATTERNS, find_limit_match, or the paused-limit path
No change to the blocked fast paths D3 added
A pane_read failure must not change which error is returned
